ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First look at the figure: the tablecloth is a square, the middle is a light-colored square, and the outside ring is a repeated diamond-shaped border. According to the rules in the figure, the whole tablecloth can be regarded as 5×5 equal small squares, among which the middle light-colored part is 3×3=9 small squares, and the border part is 25-9=16 small squares. In each border small square, the white diamond occupies half the area, so the black also occupies half the area. Thus black total area = 16×1/2 = 8 small squares, occupying 8/25 = 32% of the whole tablecloth.

raw_record.question_text: Anastasia's tablecloth has a regular pattern, as shown in the diagram. What percentage of her tablecloth is black?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as an outer square tablecloth divided by the regular spacing of the diamond pattern into a 5-by-5 grid of equal square units. The central light square occupies the middle 3-by-3 block. The remaining 16 unit squares form the patterned border. In each border unit square, the light diamond is a square rotated 45 degrees whose diagonals span the unit square, so it takes half the unit-square area and the surrounding black takes the other half. Thus black area is 16 × 1/2 = 8 unit squares out of 25 total unit squares, giving 8/25 = 32%.

method.method_draft: Use a complementary-area approach. From the image, the regular pattern shows the whole tablecloth as a 5-unit by 5-unit square, with a central nonblack square of side 3 units. So the central light area is 9/25 of the tablecloth. Around it are 16 congruent light diamonds, each inscribed in one 1-by-1 border square and therefore each having area 1/2 square unit. Their combined nonblack area is 16 × 1/2 = 8 square units. Total nonblack area is 9 + 8 = 17 square units out of 25, so black area is 25 − 17 = 8 square units. Therefore the black percentage is 8/25 = 32%.
